findings.message: PHP image tag 8.3.36-cli meets upstream threshold; tag alone does not prove deployed runtime safety
Session upload progress enabled; disabling is a partial mitigation, not a patch
Finite PHP memory limit observed; PHP project describes administrative -1 as a partial mitigation
5 POST 5xx responses from client-2d459f9e8eb3 on one path
Session progress marker visible in logged metadata: client-1a17a4b9dec7
PHP/server OOM-like diagnostic; correlate with HTTP activity
Possible web/PHP worker crash; inspect worker lifecycle
Web/PHP process spawned a utility: php-fpm8.3 -> sh; investigate context

limitations: Static Dockerfile/Compose review only; no image was pulled, built or executed.
An image tag alone is not proof of the PHP version deployed or vendor backport state.
Custom PHP builds, templating, ARG-based references and external image dependencies require manual inventory.
Configuration files may not be loaded by the active PHP SAPI or may be overridden.
No php.ini configuration completely mitigates PHP2Shell. Update runtime and restart workers.
These observations are informational and do not establish vulnerability or safety.
Scanned 11 lines; no exploit payloads or HTTP requests were generated.
Heuristic matches are triage signals, never proof of PHP2Shell compromise.
Default client identifiers are hashed; queries, cookies, POST bodies and raw error lines are not exported.
Content within multipart POST bodies is usually absent from standard access logs.
Combined findings are separate evidence streams. Correlation and remediation are human decisions.
